The [standard](standard.html) records the rules; this page records why they
are what they are. It covers what converting real deposits showed, the design
choices the first drafts left open and how each was ruled, and the questions
an ecologist's view would most help with. The full alternatives considered
are in the superseded
[`standard_draft.md`](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/blob/main/standard_draft.md).

## What building the corpus showed

**It round-trips.** Six datasets bundled with R packages, covering
single-season occupancy, N-mixture, removal sampling, CJS, dynamic occupancy
and a 158-species community dataset, convert to the format, validate, convert
back to identical arrays, and give identical model estimates in `unmarked`,
`marked` and NIMBLE on native and reconstructed data. The only things lost are
covariate values at surveys that never happened and units that were never
surveyed, which matter to no likelihood but need a side table if the sampling
frame matters.

**Real deposits behave.** The corpus now holds `r s$n_tables` tables from
`r s$n_deposits` public deposits and `r s$n_packages` textbook datasets, one
script per source. The first twenty deposits, from Dryad, Zenodo,
figshare, Dataverse and ScienceBase (30 tables with the six package datasets
then included), settled the questions below. The explicit-zero rule was
never ambiguous where the source deposited a matrix: blank meant "not
surveyed" and 0 "not detected", and in three deposits the pattern could be
cross-checked against an effort table. It was ambiguous where the source was a
record table with no survey list, so every table now declares what its survey
set rests on (`surveyEvidence`), and three tables carry a set reconstructed by
a stated rule. Coarsening was needed twice, for an Endangered tapir deposited with exact
camera coordinates and for a bird community that includes Vulnerable taxa. A
multi-state loon table fit with `y` as a species-specific state code. A MARK
input file with losses on capture exercised the `obs_removed` encoding.
Covariates that were really model outputs were dropped and logged. The
stretched designs, binned distance sampling, dependent double-observer
counts, spatial capture-recapture with a trap key, and eDNA with site, sample
and qPCR replicate as three nested levels, all fit, each with its semantics
declared in the metadata rather than implied by the columns.

**The data exists and is open.** Dryad alone has on the order of a thousand
hits for the core search terms, nearly all CC0, usually deposited as the very
site-by-occasion matrix the standard targets. A seed corpus of 50 to 100
tables is weeks of work; a harvested corpus of several hundred to a thousand,
most with 20 to 300 units and 2 to 12 occasions, is months. The corpus is one
of small tables, so a floor of 100 units would exclude most of ecology.

## The decisions, and how they were ruled

These are the design choices the draft left open. All were ruled on
2026-11-01, after twelve datasets had been through the pipeline, and the
standard was frozen as v1.0-draft. The ruling follows each item. Two later
rulings, made when the eDNA tables arrived, are listed after them.

1. **What plays the role of the item?** The draft puts the species on
   `taxon`, so a single-species table has one taxon and many occasions and a
   community table has one row per species per survey. Putting the visit
   there instead makes every table a unit-by-visit matrix, but does not
   generalise to multi-species data. *Ruled: species on `taxon`;
   the visit view is a derived pivot.*
2. **Dense zeros or a surveys table?** The explicit-zero rule makes community
   tables large and repeats observation covariates across species. The
   alternative is Darwin Core's event-core model: a sparse detections table
   plus a surveys table. The draft recommends dense for self-containment. *Ruled: dense. Each table must also declare what the
   survey set rests on (`surveyEvidence`), because three of the second batch's
   deposits were record tables with no survey list and the set had to be
   inferred.*
3. **The sample floor** (settled). It is a reported attribute, not an intake
   rule: every table carries `sample_floor`, `meets` at 30 or more units and 2
   or more occasions, otherwise `below` with the reason, and users filter on
   it. Five of the 30 built tables are below it. One has 10 sites with 43
   species and 20 surveys each, which is why a flat unit floor was the wrong
   kind of rule for this corpus. Small tables are not sought out, but they
   ship when they come.
4. **Sensitive-species coordinates.** Coarsen by rule to a 0.1-degree grid
   with the uncertainty recorded, or drop coordinates for any flagged taxon.
   *Ruled: coarsen, never drop; a taxon is flagged by the source, by IUCN
   CR/EN/VU, or by a cited national red list.*
5. **How far to stretch.** Double-observer and binned distance sampling fit by
   using `occasion` for a category rather than a time-ordered replicate;
   spatial capture-recapture adds a `trap` index. Accept the stretched
   semantics with a declared unit kind and response type, or keep
   version 1 to the families where the format is unforced. *Ruled: three lists.
   Removal, double-observer and binned distance sampling are in as declared
   stretches with their metadata required; spatial capture-recapture,
   multi-scale and per-detection designs are experimental.*
6. **A fourth nesting level.** eDNA designs can have watershed, site, sample
   and qPCR replicate. *Ruled: three levels in the key (`cluster_id`, `unit`,
   `occasion`); a fourth is a `unit_<group>` covariate, so the deposit stays
   one table.*
7. **Confirmation surveys.** False-positive models pair an uncertain method
   with a certain one. *Ruled: the certain method is a `unit_` covariate when
   it sits above the rows, or an `obs_method` value when the two share a
   level, and `detectionCertainty` in the metadata says which.*

## Open questions

The project would benefit most from an ecologist's view on four things.

- **Species as items.** Is anything lost by putting the species on `taxon`
  and the visit on `occasion`, for designs beyond the ones built so far?
- **The stretches.** Distance bins, observer cells and traps each borrow a
  column whose name says "time". The metadata declares the borrowing. Is that
  enough, or should those designs have their own columns?
- **The sample floor.** 30 units and 2 occasions as a reported attribute. Is
  it the right floor, and is reporting rather than excluding the right use of
  it?
- **The survey-evidence rule.** Three tables have survey sets reconstructed
  from detection spans. Should such tables ship at all, and if so is
  `surveyEvidence = inferred` a strong enough warning?

Each [table](data.html) links to the script that built it, which states the
mapping and what was left out. A reader who finds a table wrong should say so
in an [issue](https://github.com/ben-domingue/eco/issues); the
[corrections](corrections.html) page says what happens next.
